newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia extends licence of independent Zagreb radio.
newsitem.headline: Croatia extends licence of independent Zagreb radio.

text.p: The Croatian government, which was forced by mass street protests to shelve an attempt to silence a critical independent radio station, extended its broadcasting licence on Thursday, but only for two weeks.
The state news agency HINA said the telecommunications ministry renewed youth-oriented Radio 101's licence, which was due to expire on January 15, until the end of the month.

There was no immediate explanation for the limited extension. The ministry's Telecommunications Council, which last November granted Radio 101's frequency to a media tycoon, has been given until February 15 to resolve the dispute.
Zrinka Vrabec-Mojzes, editor-in-chief since Radio 101 was founded 12 years as a dissident voice in then-communist Yugoslavia, said the extension "does not leave us lots of manoeuvring space".
"We want the resignation of all Council members and we want the concession (licence) now," she said.
The decision to give the frequency to a radio station owned by media tycoon Ninoslav Pavic which had not even begun to broadcast at the time came as a bombshell.
Analysts believe influential rightists in the government decided Radio 101 had to be muzzled for years of criticism of authoritarian President Franjo Tudjman and his HDZ party.
More than 100,000 people staged Croatia's biggest post-independence protest in the main square of the capital Zagreb, demanding the reinstatement of Radio 101's licence.
The Telecommunications Council backed down and annulled its ruling after Pavic renounced the concession but has yet to come up with a long-term solution.
